benefit.name: At Home Program: Medical Benefits
benefit.amount: Per-item coverage — wheelchair seating to $9,000, lifts to $8,000, hospital bed to $4,000, scooter to $3,700, dental $700 a year, optical $150 a year, plus 100% of eligible prescription drugs and designated medical supplies through PharmaCare Plan F
benefit.summary: Medical equipment, therapies, dental and optical care, medical travel and PharmaCare Plan F for eligible children. See the assessed daily-living, direct nursing care and palliative routes below.

items: Your child is a BC resident enrolled in the Medical Services Plan.
Your child lives at home with a parent or guardian, or with an Extended Family Program caregiver.
Your child meets one of the routes listed below.

benefit.requiresNote: Your child is 17 or younger, is a BC resident enrolled in the Medical Services Plan, and lives at home with a parent or guardian or with an Extended Family Program caregiver. Medical-benefit routes are alternatives: assessed dependence in at least three of eating, dressing, toileting and washing; eligibility for Nursing Support Services direct nursing care, without an eligibility assessment; or a palliative condition with life expectancy of up to six months as indicated by a physician or nurse practitioner, without an eligibility assessment.
benefit.note: Benefits last until the last day of the month your child turns 18. PharmaCare Plan F coverage ends the same day. Start the adult disability assistance application about six months before that birthday. Young people in the program get a streamlined route into it. New families can still apply until March 2027.

detail.about: Medical Benefits can cover approved equipment, supplies, therapies, dental, optical, medical travel, and prescription drugs and designated medical supplies at 100% through PharmaCare Plan F. The program must approve many items before they are bought, and coverage ends on the last day of the month the child turns 18.

aboutList.lead: Medical Benefits can cover approved equipment, supplies, therapies, dental, optical, medical travel, and prescription drugs and designated medical supplies at 100% through PharmaCare Plan F.
items: The program must approve many items before they are bought.
Coverage ends on the last day of the month the child turns 18.
Any one of these routes can apply: assessed dependence in at least three of eating, dressing, toileting and washing.
Eligible for Nursing Support Services direct nursing care: no eligibility assessment is required.
Palliative route: a palliative condition with life expectancy of up to six months.
A physician or nurse practitioner must indicate this palliative life expectancy.
No eligibility assessment is required for this palliative route.

steps: Complete the At Home Program application with a doctor or nurse practitioner
Attach the requested identification and functional assessments; children under 3 may be asked for extra supporting information
Send the application to the regional At Home Program office listed by the province
Take part in the in-home assessment of eating, dressing, toileting and washing if one is required
Wait for the written decision, then work with the CYSN worker or Medical Benefits branch before purchasing covered equipment or services
documents: Completed At Home Program application with parent and medical-professional sections
Identification for the child and parent or guardian
Child's Personal Health Number and proof of active MSP
Requested functional assessments such as Vineland-3, PEDI-CAT or GMFCS, when applicable
tips: Families in current pilot areas use a different Medical Benefits application route. Check the official page for your community.
Do not buy equipment, dental, optical or travel first when pre-approval is required
Start adult PWD planning about six months before the child's 18th birthday

PharmaCare Plan F is not a separate application. Once your child gets full benefits or medical benefits through the At Home Program, MCFD sends their information to PharmaCare. The drug coverage then follows automatically.
Plan F covers designated medical supplies at 100%, as well as prescription drugs. Before you keep buying a supply yourself, ask the At Home Program or your pharmacist if it is on the designated list.
detail.time: Assessment and regional review follow a complete application; no guaranteed timeline is published

values.note: per-item equipment, therapy, dental/optical, PharmaCare Plan F

meta.effort: Application + functional assessment and medical records
